summary: Mr. Shasha discusses why we focus on slavery and hardships during Leil Haseder instead of only celebrating our freedom. He uses the analogy of a Monday morning quarterback reviewing game film to explain how reflecting on past challenges and poor choices is necessary for personal growth. He connects this to the Mishna in Masekhet Pesahim about starting with disgrace and ending with glory.
questions: Why do we talk about slavery and hardship on the night of our freedom?
How does reviewing our past mistakes help us grow?
What does it mean to start with disgrace and end with glory?
How should we respond to hardships in our lives?
